newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The shekel weakened against the dollar and was stable against the basket of foreign currencies on Thursday in quiet trading amid the Jewish Passover holiday, dealers said.
"The shekel weakened against the dollar after the dollar strengthened worldwide," a dealer at Bank Leumi said.
The Bank of Israel will announce later on Thursday its monetary programme for May. Its base rate has remained at an annualised 13.9 percent since the end of February.
Trading in the shekel was over before the central bank announcement.

"The market was not affected by the impending decision on the rates," the dealer said. "The market is already taking into consideration that a cut in interest rates will be symbolic only if there will be a cut at all," the dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4020 shekels against 3.3990 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6767 shekels against 3.6787 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6972 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6962 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9799 shekels after 1.9828 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4010 shekels.
